transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-03-04 09:30 PT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Alex (CSM), Michael (Lunaris), Priya (Lunaris SRE), Tom (CPO), Elena (Data Eng)

[00:00] Jordan (AE): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda — cost/econ review from the last run, caching and batching tuned results, next steps for the 48 hour canary.
[00:12] Michael (Lunaris): yeah thanks, we've got a couple execs on the call but main ask is: can we get to predictable unit costs for our chat assistant, especially tokens per dollar across peak/steady state?
[00:25] Samira (SE): for context we ran three configs last week: hosted default (open model v1, 8-bit), hosted + prefix cache, and a dedicated quantized path (4-bit) on a small dedicated pool. we've got perf numbers and cost calc.
[00:40] Tom (CPO): can you just give the headline numbers first? tokens per dollar and any hit to latency/quality.
[00:48] Samira (SE): headline — baseline hosted gave about 120k tokens per $1 on our assumptions (this is raw token throughput normalized). with prefix/KV caching enabled we saw effective tokens per $1 jump to roughly 200-260k depending on cache hit rate; our test had a 42% prefix hit which produced ~2.1x token savings. dedicated 4-bit path improves raw tokens/sec for high concurrency but you start to see some small quality diffs on longer context.
[01:20] Priya (SRE): when you say tokens per dollar, that's across the whole request lifecycle, includes tokenization and network overhead?
[01:26] Samira (SE): yes we included tokenization overhead and avg network egress cost in the model. one caveat: the hosted baseline had conservative batching (max batch 8, latency optimized), so tokens/sec/$ there is lower for latency-first configs.
[01:40] Jordan (AE): also worth saying, batching tradeoffs were clear — if you increase batching to improve tokens/sec, p95 latency moved from ~120ms to ~220ms for our sample prompts. that's the adaptive batching vs fixed batching tradeoff.
[01:55] Elena (Data Eng): do you have numbers on throughput vs cost for adaptive batching? we want something we can plug into our SLA calculator.
[02:03] Samira (SE): rough numbers from the run:
- latency-optimized (max batch 8): 120k tokens/$, p50~70ms, p95~120ms
- throughput-optimized (max batch 32/adaptive): 260k tokens/$, p50~110ms, p95~220ms
- dedicated 4-bit pool (batch 24): 310k tokens/$, p50~95ms, p95~240-260ms (higher p95 due to queuing at peak)
[02:32] Michael: ok that's useful. so worst case p95 hits 260ms on dedicated, which might be too high for some user flows. can we do smart routing so interactive flows hit lower latency paths?
[02:42] Jordan: absolutely, smart routing by route or path is supported — we can route low-latency flows to latency-optimized hosted nodes and burst to dedicated during non-interactive batch jobs.
[02:51] Tom: how reliable are the caching numbers — 42% hit seems high, how did you measure?
[02:57] Samira: the 42% prefix hit came from running our evaluator prompts over a 48h sample; Lunaris queries tend to reuse several standard prefixes in the assistant prompts. important note: structure changes in prompts reduce hit rate. Priya, your team can help measure canonical prompt variants which will help tune cache keys.
[03:16] Priya: yeah we can extract canonical prefixes, but we need clarity on how Redwood normalizes prompts for prefix caching. is there a risk of leaking PII in cache keys?
[03:26] Samira: good callout — caching keys are MD5 hashed and we support customer-side hashing if you want client-side normalization. also we don't store raw inputs in plain text in the cache and we can integrate with your KMS if you enable private deployment.
[03:40] Michael: what about quantization quality? earlier you said 4-bit had small quality diffs. can you show examples?
[03:46] Samira: we ran a small eval suite — in 4-bit some longer-context reasoning prompts had minor coherence drops, ~2-3% on our eval metric. for short chat it's negligible. recommendation: use 4-bit for background/embedding workloads and keep 8-bit for critical chat paths, or use mixed routing.
[04:06] Jordan: also there's a cost angle — quantize + dedicated pool reduces unit cost, but you trade off deployment flexibility and some ops overhead.
[04:15] Elena: curious about caching + batching combined — what's the compounded saving?
[04:20] Samira: in our runs combined caching + batching effectively multiplied savings: with 42% cache hits and throughput batching we saw effective tokens/$ near 320k in peaks. but remember that's conditional on your workload having lots of repeated prefixes.
[04:35] Michael: do you have a spreadsheet we can review with assumptions?
[04:38] Jordan: yes Jordan: linking cost model (short link): https://rwd.co/cost-model-lunaris (will share full sheet after call). includes per-config assumptions (batch sizes, hit rates, quantization overheads).
[04:50] Priya: what's the plan for the canary? you mentioned a 48h run. will that use real traffic?
[04:55] Samira: plan is to run on a canary subset of traffic (10% of reads, no writes) for 48h with prefix caching + adaptive batching. measure tokens saved, latency percentiles, and error rates. we'll also capture model output quality metrics via the eval set.
[05:10] Tom: if the canary shows 2x tokens/$ improvement without hurting p95 beyond 150ms, we can move to a pilot on dedicated pool for peak hours.
[05:20] Michael: one blocker — procurement wants an estimate for monthly committed spend if we go dedicated. can you provide that?
[05:26] Jordan: yes Jordan will provide a committed capacity estimate (cost + recommended buffer) after we see the 48h canary. I'll run the dedicated pool sizing based on your 95th percentile QPS from the logs you provide.
[05:40] Priya: note — our traffic has diurnal peaks and a 10% tail of long multi-turn sessions that inflate context and cost; we'll add those to the tokenization export.
[05:52] Samira: final technical note — adaptive batching lowers unit cost but can increase jitter; we recommend per-route latency SLOs in the router so user-facing endpoints keep strict p95 targets while background tasks use throughput paths.
[06:05] Jordan: recap: 1) Samira enable prefix cache + adaptive batching on canary; 2) Priya export 24h traffic sample and canonical prefixes; 3) Jordan share cost model + dedicated estimate; 4) schedule deep-dive next week.
[06:20] Michael: sounds good. thanks all.
[06:24] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the sheet and a calendar invite for the infra deep-dive.

(Automatic transcription notes: occasional word swaps, e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache; some speaker labels may be abbreviated.)
